request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Patient name]

DOB: [Patient date of birth]

Medical Record Number: [Patient's medical record number]

Admission Date: [Date of admission]

Discharge Date: [Date of discharge]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain and was diagnosed with an ectopic pregnancy in the right adnexa. A laparoscopic right salpingectomy was performed, and regular obstetric follow-up was done for the intrauterine pregnancy. The baby was delivered via spontaneous vaginal delivery at term with no significant complications.

Discharge Instructions:

The patient is advised to continue with regular obstetric follow-up and to report any signs of complications immediately. Post-operative pain management should be done as prescribed. The patient should have a healthy diet and stay hydrated, and avoid strenuous physical activity until cleared by the obstetrician. 

Follow-up:

The patient is advised to schedule a follow-up appointment with their obstetrician as soon as possible.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The hospital course describes a right adnexal ectopic pregnancy treated with laparoscopic salpingectomy, plus an intrauterine pregnancy that went to term and delivered. This suggests a heterotopic pregnancy, but the summary is ambiguous. The episode of admitted care described is the emergency presentation with abdominal pain, where the ectopic pregnancy was diagnosed and treated surgically. The term delivery is described as a separate event, probably a later admission, and it falls outside this episode.

The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is the ectopic pregnancy. ICD-10-AM places it in O00 (Ectopic pregnancy), and a tubal pregnancy codes to O00.1. The three-character category is O00.

A heterotopic pregnancy would also code to O00.8 or O00.1 with additional codes, so O00 holds either way.

CODE: O00
